shared_elements: bearded male figure shown in profile facing right
long beard rendered as rows/registers of tight curls and beaded strands
hair/headdress with a banded fillet and rows of curls at the nape
fringed and patterned garment across the shoulder/chest
wing-like feathered element rising behind the shoulder
low-relief carving on a rectangular slab
justification: Both show the same highly specific figure type: a bearded male in strict right-facing profile with a banded headdress, large ear ornament, beard built from stacked registers of beaded curls, a bossed necklace and a fringed garment, with a feathered wing element springing behind the shoulder and a rosette-like disc ornament. The main difference in depicted content is that A shows the wings much more fully spread and includes a second body/arm area with the rosette clearly on the wrist, while B's panel is dominated by the head and shoulder with the wing barely emerging — a difference of framing and completeness rather than of iconographic scheme.
